courses.title: Biology and Society
courses.description: [GE 5B] Fundamental concepts in biology are taught using socially relevant themes. Biological concepts are related to the major themes of evolution; structure and function; information flow, exchange and storage; transformations of energy and matter; and systems. Uses the study of biology to illustrate science as a way of knowing, the methods and practices of science, limits of scientific endeavors, ethics associated with biological investigations, and how biology can help inform decisions we make as individuals and as a society.

courses.title: Biology and Society Laboratory
courses.description: [GE 5C] A laboratory support course applying lecture concepts through hands-on, inquiry-based, learn-by-doing approaches. Supports students in majors that require fundamental concepts of biology as they relate to the major themes of evolution; structure and function; information flow exchange and storage; transformations of energy and matter; and systems. Uses the study of biology to illustrate science as a way of knowing, the methods and practices of science, limits of scientific endeavors, ethics associated with biological investigation, and how biology can help inform decisions we make as individuals and as a society. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1110 or BIO 1150 ; BIO 1150 can be concurrent. Pre or Corequisite(s):

courses.title: Human Anatomy
courses.description: A systemic approach to the gross and microscopic anatomy of all eleven systems of the human body. Relevant to students pursuing careers in human health. Corequisite(s): BIO 2340L .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L ; or BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Human Anatomy Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory emphasizing systemic anatomy, focusing on the structures and organs of the human body. Students are required to learn and understand the structures using: standard anatomical skeletal and organ models, hands-on experience with clay muscle models, and dissection of preserved specimens (sheep brain, sheep heart, cow eye, and cat). Corequisite(s): BIO 2340 .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L , or BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Human Physiology
courses.description: Introduction to organ-systems of the human body with emphasis on homeostatic mechanisms. Underlying cellular and molecular mechanisms are discussed within the context of integrative human physiology. Corequisite(s): BIO 2350L .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L , or BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Human Physiology Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory-based, hands-on learning of human physiology principles, techniques, and data acquisition equipment to reinforce and augment topics covered in the co-requisite lecture component. Corequisite(s): BIO 2350 .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L , or BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Introduction to Kinesiology and Health Promotion
courses.description: Introduction to the discipline, fundamental concepts, theories, history, methods, and research within kinesiology and health promotion.

courses.title: Biomechanics
courses.description: Introduction to basic mechanical and anatomical principles of human movement in sports and exercise. Corequisite(s): KIN 2040L .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 2340 and BIO 2340L .

courses.title: Biomechanics Laboratory
courses.description: Applications of biomechanics concepts to the real world using the laboratory technologies of human measurement and the application of biomechanical principles in human movement analysis. Corequisite(s): KIN 2040 .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 2340 and BIO 2340L .

courses.title: Applied Health and Well-Being
courses.description: This course addresses the issues pertaining to health behaviors including theory of behavior change, dimensions of health and wellness (e.g., mental, physical, environmental, social) and health communication.

courses.title: Movement Education for Diverse Populations
courses.description: Introduction to the fundamental dimensions of an effective movement educator needed by all kinesiology and health promotion majors. Key aspects of effective teaching and learning are explored (e.g., teaching styles, feedback, demonstrations, assessment, cultural competency).

courses.title: Contemporary Issues in Health and Human Movement
courses.description: Contemporary sociocultural issues pertaining to health and human movement. It critically explores how diversity appears in the field of kinesiology and health promotion.
courses.prerequisites: Kinesiology major.

courses.title: Foundations of Adapted Physical Activity
courses.description: Introduction to various disability concepts, such as atypical growth, development, and motor functions, legal mandates, and models of disability/inclusion. Particular focus will be placed on adapted movements for maximum inclusion. Corequisite(s): KIN 2460AS .
courses.prerequisites: Kinesiology major.

courses.title: Exercise Physiology
courses.description: Aerobic and anaerobic energy sources for muscular activity, neuromuscular physiology and function, and cardiopulmonary/respiratory physiology and function as it relates to exercise. Examples include physiological and metabolic adaptations to resistance and endurance training, nutritional and ergogenic aspects of human performance, environmental impact on exercise performance, and hormonal response to exercise. Corequisite(s): KIN 3030L .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 2350 and BIO 2350L .

courses.title: Exercise Physiology Laboratory
courses.description: Test and measure human performance including anaerobic and aerobic capacity, muscular kinematics, biometrics, and body composition. Corequisite(s): KIN 3030 .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 2350 and BIO 2350L .

courses.title: Motor Behavior
courses.description: This course examines typical and atypical motor development, motor control, and motor learning across the lifespan in the context of human movement. 3-hour lecture/discussion. Corequisite(s): KIN 3620A .
courses.prerequisites: Kinesiology major; KIN 2040 , KIN 3030 , or KIN 3040; and KIN 2040L , KIN 3030 L, or KIN 3040L.

courses.title: Motor Behavior Activity
courses.description: This course provides foundational level exposure to typical and atypical motor development, motor control, and motor learning through various activities. One two-hour activity. Corequisite(s): KIN 3620 .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2040 , KIN 3030 , or KIN 3040; and KIN 2040L , KIN 3030L , or KIN 3040L.

courses.title: Philosophical and Ethical Issues in Health and Human Movement
Nutrition, Science and Health
courses.description: [GE 5D] Integrative approach to nutrition, health, and fitness based on physiological and biochemical principles. Role of diet and other influences in promoting wellness and preventing degenerative diseases. Nutritional self-assessment project/weekly assignments/current controversies, submitted online typed discussions/assignments.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Statistics with Applications
courses.description: [GE 2] Sample and population data; descriptive statistics, including numerical and graphical summarization of central tendency and spread; elementary probability, including events, basic probability rules, binomial and normal distributions; inferential statistics, including confidence intervals and hypothesis tests for one-population mean and proportion problems, simple linear regression and correlation
courses.prerequisites: Category I, Category II, ALEKS >=46, C or better in a GE Sub-area 2/B4 course, or C- or better or CR in MAT 1051 .

courses.title: Introduction to Physical Education Teacher Education
courses.description: Prospective teachers are introduced to current practices in planning and teaching lessons, teacher behaviors, teacher qualifications, professional development, and career opportunities in physical education.

courses.title: Standards and Assessment
courses.description: Development of the skills and knowledge necessary to effectively create and administer various forms of standards-based assessment in K-12 general and adapted physical education settings. The focus is on creating engaging lessons, developing effective assessments, and collecting data to monitor student progress and growth.

courses.title: Elementary Physical Education
courses.description: Provides opportunities to explore skills and methods for teaching elementary physical education. Emphasis on standards based physical education activities with the use of Physical Education Model Content Standards for California Public Schools. Corequisite(s): KIN 3100A .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2220 , KIN 2230 , and KIN 2460 /AS, or permission of the instructor.

courses.title: Elementary Physical Education Activity
courses.description: Demonstrate skills and methods for teaching elementary physical education. Emphasis on standards based physical education activities with the use of Physical Education Model Content Standards for California Public Schools. Corequisite(s): KIN 3100 .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2220 , KIN 2230 , and KIN 2460 /AS, or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Secondary Physical Education - 1
courses.description: Application of principles, methods, strategies and practices for teaching fitness, rhythms and dance, gymnastics and self-defense through the integration of the Physical Education Model Content Standards for California Public Schools and California Teacher Performance Expectations.
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2220 - Introduction to Physical Education Teacher Education (3) KIN 2220, KIN 2230, KIN 2460, and KIN 2460AS.

courses.title: Secondary Physical Education-1 Activity
courses.description: Applies principles, methods, strategies and practices for teaching fitness, rhythms and dance, gymnastics and self-defense through the integration of the Physical Education Model Content Standards for California Public Schools and California Teacher Performance Expectations. Corequisite(s): KIN 3110 .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2220 , KIN 2230 , KIN 2460 , and KIN 2460AS .

courses.title: Secondary Physical Education - 2
courses.description: Identification of principles, methods, strategies, and practices for teaching individual, dual, team, and racket sports through the integration of the Physical Education Model Content Standards for California Public Schools and California Teacher Performance Expectations. Corequisite(s): KIN 3120A .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2220 , KIN 2230 , and KIN 2460/AS .

courses.title: Secondary Physical Education Activity - 2
courses.description: Application of principles, methods, strategies and practices for teaching individual, dual, team, and racket sports through the integration of the Physical Education Model Content Standards for California Public Schools and California Teacher Performance Expectations. Corequisite(s): KIN 3120 .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2220 , KIN 2230 , and KIN 2460/AS .

courses.title: Teaching Aquatics
courses.description: Introduction to the safety protocols and strategies to teach beginner to advanced swimming skills in secondary physical education. Corequisite(s): KIN 3130A .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2220 and KIN 2230 .

courses.title: Teaching Aquatics Activity
courses.description: In-water applications of skills and strategies to teach beginner to advanced swimming skills in secondary physical education. Corequisite(s): KIN 3130 .

courses.title: Outdoor and Adventure Education
courses.description: Provides physical education teacher education (PETE) students with the skills and strategies necessary for creating inclusive outdoor and adventure education activities. Theoretical topics include group facilitation, program design, planning, frontloading and debriefing principles, psychosocial principles, and risk management. Corequisite(s): KIN 3140A .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2220 - Introduction to Physical Education Teacher Education (3) KIN 2220 , KIN 2230 , KIN 2460 , and KIN 2460AS .

courses.title: Outdoor and Adventure Education Activity
courses.description: Prepares PETE students to design and deliver inclusive outdoor and adventure education. Emphasis placed on facilitation, program design, planning, debriefing, psychosocial principles, and risk management. Includes applied teaching experience by creating, leading, and reflecting on activities, strengthening leadership, instructional practice, and adaptive strategies for physical education. Corequisite(s): KIN 3140 .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2220 - Introduction to Physical Education Teacher Education (3) KIN 2220 , KIN 2230 , KIN 2460 , and KIN 2460AS .

courses.title: Applied Adapted Physical Education
courses.description: Evaluation of instructional strategies, assessments, progress monitoring, and behavior management strategies to implement when teaching students with disabilities. Corequisite(s): KIN 3460A .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2220 - Introduction to Physical Education Teacher Education (3) KIN 2220 , KIN 2230 , KIN 2460 , and KIN 2460AS .

courses.title: Applied Adapted Physical Education Activity
courses.description: Application of supervised clinical teaching of adapted physical education to participants with disabilities at the Cal Poly Pomona Motor Development Clinic (MDC). Students will learn the MDC operational processes. Corequisite(s): KIN 3460 .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2220 , KIN 2230 , and KIN 2460/AS .
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 4 units, with a maximum of 2 units per semester.

courses.title: Social and Historical Perspectives in Kinesiology
Cal Poly Pomona Undergraduate Sponsored Summer Experience
courses.description: Enrollment in this 0-unit course allows students to receive university services while participating in a Cal Poly Pomona sponsored summer experience.
